chapters.title: Linux History & Foundations
chapters.desc: From Unix and GNU to Torvalds, distros and the kernel's job

questions.q: Who created the Linux kernel?
questions.e: Linus Torvalds announced the Linux kernel in 1991 as a student in Finland.

questions.q: Linux itself is technically a...
questions.e: Linux names the kernel, the layer between programs and hardware. A distribution adds tools and apps; some distributions do not use GNU tools.

questions.q: In which year was the Linux kernel first released?
questions.e: Torvalds posted the first public release, version 0.01, in September 1991.

questions.q: The Linux kernel is licensed under...
questions.e: Linux kernel source is distributed under GPL-2.0-only, with a syscall exception; redistribution of modified kernel code has license conditions. Think kernel license, not every Linux app.

questions.q: Who founded the GNU Project?
questions.e: Richard Stallman started GNU in 1983 to build a free Unix-like OS.

questions.q: GNU is a recursive acronym meaning...
questions.e: GNU stands for 'GNU's Not Unix' - a hacker's recursive joke.

questions.q: Which of these is a Linux distribution?
questions.e: Ubuntu is a Debian-based Linux distro; Solaris and FreeBSD are Unix-like but not Linux.

questions.q: The official Linux mascot is...
questions.e: Tux the penguin is the Linux mascot, chosen by Linus Torvalds.

questions.q: Unix, which inspired Linux, was originally developed at...
questions.e: Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie built Unix at AT&T's Bell Labs in 1969.

questions.q: Android is built on top of which kernel?
questions.e: Android uses a modified Linux kernel under its own user space.

questions.q: What is a shell in Linux?
o: The outer case of the server
A command-line interpreter between user and kernel
questions.e: The shell reads your commands and asks the kernel to run them.

questions.q: On many traditional Linux distributions, which shell is commonly the default interactive shell?
questions.e: bash is common on Debian, Ubuntu and many server installations. Defaults vary by distro and account; check your own with getent passwd "$USER".

questions.q: The main job of the Linux kernel is to...
o: Manage hardware resources like CPU, memory and devices
questions.e: The kernel schedules CPU work, manages memory and devices. It is not the same thing as a shell or desktop.

questions.q: Open source software means...
o: Anyone can sell it as their own
Source code can be viewed, modified and shared
The software is always free of cost
questions.e: Open source licenses grant rights to read, modify and redistribute code.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a Linux distribution?
questions.e: Apache is a web server; Debian, Fedora and Arch are distros.

questions.q: Ubuntu is based on which distribution?
questions.e: Ubuntu is built from Debian's unstable/testing branches.

questions.q: Which distribution is built from Red Hat Enterprise Linux sources?
questions.e: AlmaLinux is built from RHEL sources for binary compatibility. It is not necessarily a bit-for-bit or 1:1 rebuild of every RHEL package.

questions.q: Arch Linux follows which release model?
questions.e: Arch is rolling: you install once and keep updating forever.

questions.q: The apt package manager belongs to which distro family?
questions.e: apt manages .deb packages on Debian, Ubuntu and their derivatives.

questions.q: Which command shows the running kernel version?
questions.e: uname -r prints the kernel release, e.g. 5.15.0-91-generic.

questions.q: A Linux distribution bundles the kernel with...
o: GNU tools, package manager and applications
questions.e: Distro = Linux kernel + GNU utilities + package management + apps.

questions.q: Linus Torvalds said he was inspired by which teaching OS?
questions.e: Andrew Tanenbaum's MINIX inspired Torvalds to write his own kernel.

questions.q: According to recent TOP500 lists, which OS family dominates the top 500 supercomputers?
questions.e: Linux dominates TOP500 systems. This is a changing ranking, so check the latest list rather than memorizing a permanent 100% claim.

questions.q: Which of these is a Linux desktop environment?
questions.e: GNOME (like KDE Plasma or XFCE) is a full desktop environment.

questions.q: The GPL's 'copyleft' rule means...
o: Derivative works must stay under the same license
questions.e: GPL copyleft applies when you distribute covered derivative code: recipients get the same GPL rights. Private changes need not be published just because you made them.

chapters.title: Navigation & the Filesystem
chapters.desc: pwd, cd, ls and where everything lives: /etc, /var, /home...

questions.q: Which command prints your current directory?
questions.e: pwd = print working directory.

questions.q: How do you jump straight to your home directory?
questions.e: cd with no argument or cd ~ lands in your home directory.

questions.q: The top of the Linux filesystem tree is...
questions.e: Everything hangs off the single root directory '/'.

questions.q: Which ls option also shows hidden files?
questions.e: -a (all) includes dotfiles like .bashrc.

questions.q: Which option gives a long listing with permissions and owner?
questions.e: ls -l shows type, permissions, owner, size and mtime.

questions.q: How do you show file sizes in human-readable form (K, M, G)?
questions.e: -h makes sizes human readable; combine with -l.

questions.q: Which command moves you one directory up?
questions.e: '..' always means the parent directory.

questions.q: Which of these paths is absolute as written (before shell expansion)?
questions.e: An absolute path starts with /. ~/data is expanded to a home-directory path by some shells, but the literal path does not start with /.

questions.q: Hidden files in Linux start with...
questions.e: Files like .profile are hidden from plain ls.

questions.q: System-wide configuration files live in...
questions.e: /etc holds configs like /etc/passwd and /etc/fstab.

questions.q: Logs and other constantly changing data belong in...
questions.e: /var = variable data: logs, caches, spool.

questions.q: Regular users' home directories are usually under...
questions.e: Users get /home/username; root alone gets /root.

questions.q: Files in /tmp are intended for...
o: Temporary data that may be deleted by cleanup policy
questions.e: /tmp is temporary scratch space. Cleanup timing depends on the system; do not depend on its contents surviving a reboot.

questions.q: According to the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard, which path is for essential system-administration binaries?
questions.e: /sbin historically held essential admin commands. On merged-/usr systems it may be a symlink to /usr/sbin.

questions.q: /proc is...
o: A virtual filesystem exposing kernel and process info
questions.e: /proc is generated on the fly by the kernel; try cat /proc/cpuinfo.

questions.q: Device files like /dev/sda are found in...
questions.e: /dev holds special files representing hardware devices.

questions.q: According to the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard, where do shareable, read-only system programs and data primarily belong?
questions.e: /usr contains many binaries, libraries and shareable data. Local administrator-installed software often goes under /usr/local instead.

questions.q: What does 'cd -' do?
o: Jumps back to the previous directory
questions.e: cd - toggles to the last directory you were in.

questions.q: In paths, '~' expands to...
questions.e: At the start of a shell word, ~ normally expands to the current user’s home directory. This is shell expansion, not a literal filesystem path.

questions.q: Linux filenames are generally...
questions.e: ext4 and friends treat File.txt and file.txt as two files.

questions.q: Which command finds files by name under a directory tree?
questions.e: find walks the tree; -name matches the filename.

questions.q: In the traditional Unix saying, many resources are represented as a...
questions.e: The Unix idea is to expose many resources through file-like interfaces, for example devices under /dev. It is a useful model, not a literal claim about every object.

questions.q: Which command shows how much space a directory uses?
questions.e: du -sh summarizes disk usage; df is for whole filesystems.

questions.q: The path separator on Linux is...
questions.e: Linux uses / ; backslash is an escape character in the shell.

questions.q: A single dot '.' in a path refers to...
questions.e: . = here, .. = one level up.

chapters.title: File & Directory Management
chapters.desc: mkdir, cp, mv, rm, links and finding anything

questions.q: Which command creates a new directory?
questions.e: mkdir projects creates the directory 'projects'.

questions.q: What does mkdir -p /a/b/c do?
questions.e: -p makes the whole chain and never errors if it exists.

questions.q: On a nonexistent path, touch normally creates what?
o: Create an empty file or update its timestamp
questions.e: touch creates an empty file if it does not exist. For an existing file, it changes timestamps instead of emptying it.

questions.q: Copy file1.txt to backup.txt with...
questions.e: cp leaves the original in place; mv would rename.

questions.q: Copying a whole directory tree requires...
questions.e: -r (recursive) descends into subdirectories.

questions.q: Which command both moves and renames files?
questions.e: mv old new renames; mv file dir/ moves.

questions.q: Delete a file with...
questions.e: rm removes the file immediately - no trash bin.

questions.q: rmdir works only when the directory is...
questions.e: rmdir refuses to remove non-empty directories; use rm -r for those.

questions.q: rm -r is used to...
o: Delete directories and their contents recursively
questions.e: rm -r deletes the directory and everything inside it.

questions.q: What makes rm -rf dangerous on a wrong path?
o: It force-deletes everything without asking, no undo
questions.e: -r descends into directories; -f suppresses many prompts. GNU rm protects the literal / by default, not every dangerous typo.

questions.q: Create a symbolic (soft) link with...
questions.e: ln -s makes a symlink; plain ln makes a hard link.

questions.q: For a regular file on the same filesystem, why can a hard link still access its data after another name is removed?
o: It shares the same inode, so it survives target deletion
questions.e: Both names point to one inode. Removing one directory entry does not remove file data while another hard link remains.

questions.q: Which command identifies a file's real type regardless of extension?
questions.e: file inspects magic bytes, e.g. 'report' could be a PDF without .pdf.

questions.q: Which tool looks up file paths using a periodically updated database (when installed)?
questions.e: locate/plocate uses a file-name index updated by updatedb. It can be stale and is not installed everywhere.

questions.q: With GNU find, which command matches files whose size rounds up to more than 100 units of 1 MiB under /home?
questions.e: GNU find -size +100M uses 1 MiB units rounded up; it is not exactly the same as a strict >100 MiB byte comparison. Add -type f to exclude directories.

questions.q: Which command looks up a command on PATH and prints an executable path when found?
questions.e: which searches PATH for an executable; e.g. which python3 may print /usr/bin/python3. Shell aliases/functions need separate inspection with type.

questions.q: Rename notes.txt to todo.txt using...
questions.e: mv handles renames within the same directory.

questions.q: Which cp option preserves permissions and timestamps like an archive copy?
questions.e: -a (archive) keeps mode, ownership, timestamps and recurses.

questions.q: Show a one-line total size of /var/log with...
questions.e: -s summarizes, -h humanizes.

questions.q: Which command counts newline characters in a file?
questions.e: wc -l counts newline characters, usually called lines. A final line without a newline is not added to this count.

questions.q: Which tool shows line-by-line differences between two text files?
questions.e: diff compares lines and prints changes; e.g. diff -u old.txt new.txt uses unified format. cmp checks bytes instead.

questions.q: Create directories logs, data and backup in one shot with...
questions.e: mkdir accepts multiple names in one command.

questions.q: Running 'cp report.txt ~/docs/' when docs exists will...
o: Place report.txt inside ~/docs with the same name
questions.e: When the destination is a directory, cp copies into it keeping the name.

questions.q: When mv moves a regular file across filesystems, what does it usually do?
o: Copies it then deletes the original
questions.e: rename cannot cross filesystems, so GNU mv typically copies data and removes the original after a successful copy. This is not an atomic rename.

questions.q: Which command shows full metadata of a file - inode, size, permissions, timestamps?
questions.e: stat reports inode number, links, access/modify/change times and more.

chapters.title: Viewing & Working with Text
chapters.desc: cat, less, grep, pipes and redirection - the daily toolkit

questions.q: Print an entire file to the terminal with...
questions.e: cat dumps the whole file at once - best for short files.

questions.q: The best command to page through a long file interactively is...
questions.e: less scrolls forward and backward without loading everything at once.

questions.q: Show the first 10 lines of a file with...
questions.e: head defaults to the first 10 lines.

questions.q: Show the last 10 lines of a file with...
questions.e: tail defaults to the last 10 lines - perfect for recent log entries.

questions.q: Watch a growing log file live with...
questions.e: tail -f follows the file and prints new lines as they arrive.

questions.q: Print the first 20 lines with...
questions.e: head -n 20 prints at most 20 lines from the start. On GNU head, older -20 syntax may also work, so it is not a useful wrong option.

questions.q: Count lines, words and bytes with...
questions.e: wc = word count; wc -l is the classic line counter.

questions.q: Search for the word 'error' inside a file with...
questions.e: grep prints lines matching the pattern.

questions.q: grep -i does what?
questions.e: -i matches ERROR, error, Error alike.

questions.q: Search a pattern in every file under a directory with...
questions.e: -r recurses through subdirectories.

questions.q: grep -v pattern shows...
questions.e: -v inverts: it prints the non-matching lines.

questions.q: Which grep option prints line numbers?
questions.e: grep -n error app.log prefixes each hit with its line number.

questions.q: The pipe symbol | does what?
o: Sends one command's output into another's input
questions.e: ps aux | grep nginx feeds ps output into grep.

questions.q: Redirect output to a file, overwriting it, with...
questions.e: > truncates and writes; >> appends.

questions.q: Append output to an existing file with...
questions.e: >> keeps old content and adds to the end.

questions.q: Redirect only error messages (stderr) with...
questions.e: File descriptor 2 is stderr; 1 is stdout.

questions.q: In a POSIX-style shell, which form redirects both stdout and stderr to all.txt?
questions.e: The shell opens all.txt for stdout, then 2>&1 sends stderr to that same destination. Order matters: command 2>&1 > all.txt behaves differently.

questions.q: Inside less, how do you search for text?
questions.e: /pattern searches forward, ?pattern searches backward, n repeats.

questions.q: How do you quit less?
questions.e: q quits; Ctrl+C only interrupts operations.

questions.q: cat -n does what?
questions.e: cat -n prefixes each line with its number.

questions.q: Which sort option compares lines by numeric value rather than lexically?
questions.e: sort -n puts 9 before 10 by comparing leading numbers. Plain sort compares text and may put 10 first.

questions.q: uniq -c is usually combined with sort because...
o: uniq only collapses adjacent duplicate lines
questions.e: sort file | uniq -c counts how often each distinct line appears.

questions.q: For a simple comma-delimited file with no quoted commas, how can you print field 2?
questions.e: cut -d, -f2 uses comma as delimiter. Real CSV allows quoted commas and needs a CSV-aware parser.

questions.q: Print just the first whitespace-separated column with...
questions.e: awk splits on whitespace by default; $1 is the first field.

questions.q: Add the line 'backup done' to the end of run.log without opening an editor...
questions.e: echo plus >> appends the line instantly.

questions.q: In rwx, the letters stand for...
questions.e: r=read, w=write, x=execute (or enter, for directories).

questions.q: Permission 755 means...
questions.e: 7=rwx for owner, 5=r-x for group and others.

questions.q: chmod 644 file.txt gives...
questions.e: 6=rw for owner, 4=r for group and others - typical for web files.

questions.q: Which command adds execute permission to script.sh without replacing its existing read/write bits?
questions.e: chmod +x adds execute bits subject to umask; chmod 111 replaces other permissions. If you need only the owner, use chmod u+x.

questions.q: Change owner and group of a file with...
questions.e: chown sets owner; user:group sets both at once.

questions.q: User account information (name, UID, shell) is stored in...
questions.e: /etc/passwd is world-readable; no password hashes live there.

questions.q: On a typical Linux system with shadow passwords, where are local password hashes kept?
questions.e: /etc/shadow stores local password hashes on systems using shadow passwords. Access is restricted; centralized logins may not store hashes locally.

questions.q: Group definitions live in...
questions.e: /etc/group lists group name, GID and members.

questions.q: Which command prints your current username?
questions.e: whoami answers 'who am I' with your effective username.

questions.q: Show your UID, GID and all groups with...
questions.e: id prints uid, gid and every group you belong to.

questions.q: On a configured sudo system, which command normally runs command as root?
questions.e: sudo command runs as root by default when your sudo policy allows it. sudo -u otheruser selects another account.

questions.q: Switch to another user account entirely with...
questions.e: su - opens a login shell as that user (their password needed).

questions.q: Create a new user account with...
questions.e: useradd is the low-level tool; adduser is the friendlier Debian wrapper.

questions.q: Set or change a user's password with...
questions.e: passwd akash prompts for the new password interactively.

questions.q: Remove a user account with...
questions.e: userdel deletes the account; -r also removes the home directory.

questions.q: Which numeric UID has superuser privileges on Linux?
questions.e: UID 0 has superuser identity. The account named root normally has UID 0, but account names alone do not grant it.

questions.q: For ordinary users other than root, permission 700 on a directory grants which access?
o: Only the owner can enter, read or modify it
questions.e: 700 = rwx for owner and --- for group/others. The owner can list, enter and modify the directory, subject to other filesystem constraints; root can bypass ordinary mode checks.

questions.q: Ignoring root and ACLs, which class has the write bit in -rw-r--r--?
questions.e: The owner triplet rw- includes write. Group and other triplets r-- do not; root and ACLs can change effective access.

questions.q: In ls -l output, a first character of 'd' means...
questions.e: d=directory, -=regular file, l=symlink.

questions.q: A first character of 'l' in ls -l means...
questions.e: l marks a symlink, shown as link -> target.

questions.q: Given a regular file created with default mode 666 and umask 022, which mode results?
questions.e: Creation applies mode & ~umask: 0666 & ~0022 = 0644. A program may request a more restrictive starting mode.

questions.q: Which action normally requires root?
o: Changing another user's file ownership with chown
questions.e: Only root can chown files to arbitrary users.

questions.q: /etc/sudoers should be edited with...
questions.e: visudo syntax-checks before saving, so a typo can't lock you out.

questions.q: Which command lists the groups you belong to?
questions.e: groups prints your group memberships; id shows them with IDs.

questions.q: Add user akash to the sudo group on Debian/Ubuntu with...
questions.e: -aG appends a supplementary group; forgetting -a replaces all groups.

chapters.title: Processes & Job Control
chapters.desc: ps, top, kill, signals, jobs and priorities

questions.q: Which command shows a snapshot of processes with user, CPU and memory columns?
questions.e: ps aux shows a snapshot with USER, %CPU, %MEM and more. top is for a refreshing view.

questions.q: Which tool gives a live, refreshing view of processes?
questions.e: top (or htop) updates continuously; ps is a snapshot.

questions.q: PID stands for...
questions.e: Every process gets a unique numeric PID.

questions.q: PPID is...
questions.e: Each process (except PID 1) was started by a parent, recorded as PPID.

questions.q: On a Linux system using systemd as its init system, which program runs as PID 1?
questions.e: The kernel starts systemd as PID 1 on systemd-based systems. Other init systems or containers may use a different PID 1.

questions.q: The default signal sent by plain 'kill PID' is...
questions.e: SIGTERM politely asks the process to shut down and clean up.

questions.q: Which signal does kill -9 PID send?
o: Force-kills the process; it cannot be caught or ignored
questions.e: kill -9 sends SIGKILL; a program cannot catch or ignore it. An uninterruptible kernel wait may delay its exit.

questions.q: Kill processes by name instead of PID with...
questions.e: pkill matches process names; kill needs a numeric PID.

questions.q: On a typical Linux system, which command signals every process whose executable name is exactly nginx?
questions.e: killall nginx matches processes by executable name. pkill -x nginx also does this, so the offered pkill option must not be a second correct answer.

questions.q: On Linux, the user-visible nice values normally range from...
questions.e: Linux nice values run from -20 (higher scheduling priority) to 19 (lower). CPU time still depends on scheduler and other processes.

questions.q: Change the priority of an already-running process with...
questions.e: renice -n 5 -p 1234 adjusts PID 1234 on the fly.

questions.q: Run a command in the background by ending it with...
questions.e: 'longjob &' starts it in the background of your shell.

questions.q: List this shell's background jobs with...
questions.e: jobs shows job numbers like [1] Running for the current shell.

questions.q: Bring job 1 back to the foreground with...
questions.e: fg %1 resumes job 1 attached to your terminal.

questions.q: Resume a stopped job in the background with...
questions.e: bg %1 continues a Ctrl+Z'd job without the terminal.

questions.q: Ctrl+C sends which signal?
questions.e: SIGINT interrupts; programs may catch it to clean up.

questions.q: Ctrl+Z does what to the foreground process?
o: Suspends (stops) it and returns your prompt
questions.e: Ctrl+Z sends SIGTSTP; resume with fg or bg.

questions.q: Which option helps a shell-launched process ignore SIGHUP after logout?
questions.e: nohup ignores SIGHUP on logout. The final & backgrounds the command, while a service manager is better for long-running services.

questions.q: In ps aux, the 'a' option means...
o: Show processes of all users with a terminal
questions.e: a lifts the 'only your processes' restriction (for tty processes).

questions.q: A zombie process is...
o: A dead child whose exit status the parent has not collected
questions.e: Zombies hold only an exit-code entry; killing them does nothing.

questions.q: What generally adopts an orphaned process when its parent exits on modern Linux?
questions.e: Orphans are reparented to the nearest living child subreaper, if one exists, otherwise PID 1. It is not always directly PID 1.

questions.q: The three load averages displayed by uptime normally summarize which time windows?
questions.e: The windows are 1, 5 and 15 minutes. On Linux the load includes runnable and uninterruptible tasks, not just CPU use.

questions.q: Check RAM and swap usage in human-readable form with...
questions.e: free -h shows total, used, free memory plus swap.

questions.q: List all signal names and numbers with...
questions.e: kill -l prints the table: 1 HUP, 2 INT, 9 KILL, 15 TERM...

questions.q: Live details about process 1234 (memory maps, fds, status) are under...
questions.e: The kernel exposes every process as a directory under /proc/<pid>.

chapters.title: Package Management
chapters.desc: apt, dnf/yum, rpm/dpkg, pacman, snap & flatpak

questions.q: The package manager on Debian and Ubuntu is...
questions.e: apt installs .deb packages on Debian-family systems.

questions.q: Refresh the list of available packages with...
questions.e: update downloads package indexes; it does not upgrade anything yet.

questions.q: On Debian/Ubuntu, which command upgrades installed packages without normally removing installed packages?
questions.e: apt upgrade installs available upgrades but normally avoids removing installed packages; full-upgrade may remove them. Run apt update first to refresh the index.

questions.q: Install the nginx package with...
questions.e: apt install resolves dependencies and installs them automatically.

questions.q: Remove a package but keep its config files with...
questions.e: remove deletes binaries; configs in /etc stay for a later reinstall.

questions.q: Remove a package AND its configuration files with...
questions.e: purge = remove + config cleanup.

questions.q: Search available packages for 'editor' with...
questions.e: apt search scans names and descriptions of all known packages.

questions.q: Show version, size and description of a package with...
questions.e: apt show displays the package's full metadata.

questions.q: Install a downloaded .deb file with...
questions.e: dpkg -i installs a local .deb without resolving dependencies by itself. apt install ./file.deb is often easier when dependencies matter.

questions.q: Which command lists installed Debian packages and their status?
questions.e: dpkg -l shows package status and versions; it may also show removed packages with residual configs, so check the status column for ii.

questions.q: Which current command-line package manager is standard on modern Fedora and RHEL 8+?
questions.e: dnf is standard in modern Fedora/RHEL. The older yum command may remain as a compatibility entry point.

questions.q: Install httpd on a Fedora/RHEL system with...
questions.e: dnf install handles repos and dependencies like apt does.

questions.q: Which command installs a local RPM file with rpm (without automatic dependency resolution)?
questions.e: rpm -ivh installs with verbose output and progress. dnf install ./file.rpm is generally preferable when dependencies must be resolved.

questions.q: List every installed RPM package with...
questions.e: -q query, -a all: rpm -qa | grep nginx.

questions.q: Find which installed package owns /usr/bin/curl on Debian with...
questions.e: dpkg -S searches by file path; rpm -qf is the RHEL equivalent.

questions.q: Arch Linux uses which package manager?
questions.e: pacman is Arch's fast, simple package manager.

questions.q: Fully sync and upgrade an Arch system with...
questions.e: -Syu syncs databases and upgrades everything - the Arch ritual.

questions.q: Which company develops and maintains the snap packaging system?
questions.e: Canonical develops snapd and the Snap Store. Remember Canonical -> Ubuntu -> snap.

questions.q: By default, Flatpak applications are designed to run...
o: Sandboxed, isolated from most of the system
questions.e: Flatpak apps use sandbox permissions; access can be granted or overridden, so do not assume complete isolation.

questions.q: A package dependency is...
o: Another package or library the software needs to run
questions.e: apt/dnf resolve dependencies automatically; dpkg alone does not.

questions.q: A repository (repo) in package management is...
o: A server hosting packages and their metadata
questions.e: Repos are what apt update downloads its package lists from.

questions.q: Remove packages that were installed as dependencies but are no longer needed...
questions.e: autoremove clears orphaned dependencies; clean clears the download cache.

questions.q: Where can APT repository definitions be placed on Debian/Ubuntu?
questions.e: APT reads /etc/apt/sources.list and files under /etc/apt/sources.list.d/; these may be .list or modern .sources files.

questions.q: Fix broken/unmet dependencies after a failed install with...
questions.e: apt -f install pulls in or removes whatever resolves the breakage.

questions.q: Why prefer the package manager over compiling from source for most installs?
o: It handles dependencies, updates and clean removal
questions.e: Package managers track files so upgrades and uninstalls stay clean.

chapters.title: Networking Essentials
chapters.desc: ip, ping, DNS, ssh, ports and firewalls

questions.q: Show all IP addresses on the machine with...
questions.e: ip a lists every interface with its addresses.

questions.q: For managing network interface addresses, the ip command is the modern replacement for...
questions.e: ip addr replaces many ifconfig uses. ip route also replaces older route uses; the question asks specifically about addresses.

questions.q: Show the routing table with...
questions.e: ip route shows the default gateway and per-network routes.

questions.q: The default gateway is...
o: The router your machine sends outside traffic to
questions.e: Packets for unknown networks go to the default gateway.

questions.q: Test basic connectivity to 8.8.8.8 with...
questions.e: ping sends ICMP echo requests and measures round-trip time.

questions.q: DNS does what?
o: Resolves names like google.com to IP addresses
questions.e: DNS is the internet's phone book.

questions.q: Which file traditionally lists resolver nameservers, possibly as a local stub?
questions.e: /etc/resolv.conf lists resolver nameservers, though systemd-resolved or NetworkManager often manages it and may point to a local stub.

questions.q: Static hostname-to-IP mappings live in...
questions.e: /etc/hosts holds local hostname mappings. The lookup order with DNS comes from /etc/nsswitch.conf.

questions.q: Which modern command lists listening TCP and UDP sockets numerically?
questions.e: ss -tuln: -t TCP, -u UDP, -l listening, -n numeric. UDP has no LISTEN state in the TCP sense, but the option selects bound sockets.

questions.q: Which command writes the body of https://example.com to stdout by default?
questions.e: curl URL prints the response body to stdout by default; use -o file or -O to save it. wget defaults to saving a file.

questions.q: Download a file to disk non-interactively with...
questions.e: wget saves the file locally; curl -O does the same.

questions.q: Securely log into a remote Linux machine with...
questions.e: SSH encrypts the whole session; telnet sends plaintext.

questions.q: SSH listens on which port by default?
questions.e: Port 22 for SSH; 21 FTP, 23 telnet.

questions.q: HTTPS uses which port?
questions.e: 443 is HTTPS; 80 is plain HTTP.

questions.q: Which is the standard port number for DNS service?
questions.e: DNS commonly uses port 53 over UDP or TCP. DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS use other ports/protocols.

questions.q: Trace the path packets take to a host with...
questions.e: traceroute (or tracepath/mtr) shows each hop.

questions.q: Show or set the machine's name with...
questions.e: hostname prints it; hostnamectl sets it persistently.
localhost always points back at your own machine.

questions.q: Which option is an RFC 1918 private IPv4 address block?
questions.e: RFC 1918 defines 192.168.0.0/16 as private. The 100.64.0.0/10 block is shared carrier-grade address space, a different category.

questions.q: Which dotted-decimal subnet mask corresponds to an IPv4 /24 prefix?
questions.e: /24 has 24 leading 1 bits, giving 255.255.255.0. A /24 has 256 total IPv4 addresses; not every network has exactly 254 usable hosts.

questions.q: Manage NetworkManager connections from the CLI with...
questions.e: nmcli device status / nmcli connection show are daily tools on RHEL-family.

questions.q: The machine's hostname is stored persistently in...
questions.e: /etc/hostname is read at boot; hostnamectl writes it.

questions.q: Query DNS records in detail with...
questions.e: dig (or nslookup/host) queries A, MX, TXT and other records.

questions.q: On Ubuntu installations where it is installed, which tool is a simple firewall frontend?
questions.e: ufw stands for Uncomplicated Firewall. It is a frontend, not the underlying Linux firewall engine.

questions.q: Copy a file securely to another host over SSH with...
questions.e: scp (or rsync over ssh) copies through the encrypted SSH channel.

chapters.title: Disks, Filesystems & Storage
chapters.desc: df, mount, fstab, LVM, RAID and inodes

questions.q: Show free space on all mounted filesystems, human-readable...
questions.e: df = disk free, per filesystem; -h for G/M units.

questions.q: Show the total size of /var/log with...
questions.e: du -sh summarizes usage; df shows the whole filesystem.

questions.q: List block devices (disks and partitions) as a tree with...
questions.e: lsblk shows sda -> sda1/sda2 hierarchy with sizes and mountpoints.

questions.q: See the partition table of /dev/sda with...
questions.e: fdisk -l (or parted -l) prints partition layout.

questions.q: Create an ext4 filesystem on /dev/sdb1 with...
questions.e: mkfs formats - it destroys existing data on the partition.

questions.q: Attach /dev/sdb1 at /mnt/data with...
questions.e: mount grafts the filesystem into the directory tree.

questions.q: Detach a mounted filesystem with...
questions.e: It's umount (no first 'n'). It fails while files are open.

questions.q: Filesystems mounted automatically at boot are listed in...
questions.e: fstab = filesystem table: device, mountpoint, type, options.

questions.q: Find a partition's UUID with...
questions.e: blkid prints UUIDs and filesystem types for all block devices.

questions.q: Why mount by UUID in fstab instead of /dev/sdb1?
o: Device letters can change between boots
questions.e: /dev/sdX naming depends on detection order; UUIDs are stable.

questions.q: Which description best fits swap space on Linux?
o: Storage used for swapped memory pages when the kernel chooses to move them out of RAM
questions.e: Swap holds memory pages moved out of RAM by the kernel, which can happen before RAM is completely full.

questions.q: Enable a swap partition with...
questions.e: mkswap formats it first, then swapon activates it.

questions.q: What is a typical benefit of Linux Logical Volume Manager (LVM)?
o: Flexible volumes you can resize and span across disks
questions.e: LVM pools physical storage into volume groups and gives flexible logical volumes. Filesystem support and free space determine whether online growth or shrinking works.

questions.q: The LVM stacking order is...
o: Physical volumes -> volume group -> logical volumes
questions.e: Disks become PVs, PVs pool into a VG, LVs are carved from the VG.

questions.q: Initialize /dev/sdb as an LVM physical volume with...
questions.e: pvcreate labels the disk as LVM physical volume.

questions.q: Create volume group 'data' from /dev/sdb with...
questions.e: vgcreate names the pool and assigns PVs to it.

questions.q: Create a 20G logical volume 'web' in VG 'data' with...
questions.e: lvcreate -L size -n name vgname, then mkfs the new /dev/data/web.

questions.q: On an ext4 filesystem with enough free space in VG data, which command sequence grows web LV by 10G and then grows its filesystem?
questions.e: lvextend grows the logical volume; resize2fs grows ext4 afterward. XFS uses xfs_growfs instead. Verify the device and backups before changing storage.

questions.q: Which pair is a common default for Ubuntu/Debian and RHEL Linux installations respectively?
questions.e: Ubuntu/Debian commonly default to ext4; RHEL commonly uses XFS. They are not necessarily the two most common on every Linux system.

questions.q: An inode stores...
o: File metadata (permissions, blocks, times) - not the filename
questions.e: Names live in directory entries pointing at inode numbers.

questions.q: Two hard links to the same file share...
questions.e: ls -li shows identical inode numbers for hard-linked names.

questions.q: Which tool checks and can repair an unmounted filesystem using its appropriate filesystem-specific checker?
questions.e: fsck dispatches to filesystem-specific checkers; use the right tool for the filesystem and do not repair a mounted writable filesystem. XFS repair is handled separately by xfs_repair.

questions.q: Which command copies raw bytes from /dev/sda to disk.img (assuming enough destination space)?
questions.e: dd copies raw data from if= to of=. It can read an entire disk image; check source, destination and permissions carefully to avoid data loss.

questions.q: In a healthy two-disk RAID 1 mirror, what happens if one disk fails?
o: Mirroring - same data on two disks
questions.e: RAID 1 mirrors data. A healthy two-disk mirror generally keeps running after one disk fails, but RAID is no backup against deletion or corruption.

questions.q: Which option can interactively explore directory disk usage when ncdu is installed?
questions.e: ncdu lets you navigate disk usage interactively. du piped to sort is a noninteractive alternative; they should not share one answer option.

chapters.title: Shell Scripting Basics
chapters.desc: Variables, loops, tests, functions and exit codes

questions.q: Which first line selects /bin/bash when you execute a script directly on a system where bash is there?
questions.e: #!/bin/bash is a shebang that selects that interpreter. Scripts do not universally require it; bash script.sh works without an executable bit.

questions.q: Which command adds execute permission to backup.sh without running it?
questions.e: chmod +x adds the execute bit, subject to umask. Running via bash backup.sh does not require the execute bit.

questions.q: Assuming script.sh is executable with a valid interpreter, how do you run it from the current directory?
questions.e: ./ explicitly names the current directory. Most shells do not search . via PATH by default.

questions.q: Correct variable assignment in bash...
questions.e: No spaces around = ; the $ appears only when reading.

questions.q: Print the value of variable NAME with...
questions.e: $NAME expands the variable; quotes preserve spaces.

questions.q: Store a command's output in a variable with...
questions.e: $(command) is command substitution; backticks are the old form.

questions.q: Read keyboard input into a variable with...
questions.e: read name pauses and stores the typed line in $name.

questions.q: Inside a script, the first argument is...
questions.e: $1, $2... are positional parameters; $0 is the script name.

questions.q: $# contains...
questions.e: $# counts positional parameters - handy for usage checks.

questions.q: In bash, what does quoted "$@" represent?
questions.e: Quote "$@" to keep each argument separate, including names with spaces; without quotes bash splits arguments further.

questions.q: Immediately after a command completes in bash, what does $? contain?
o: The exit status of the last command
questions.e: $? is the exit status of the most recently completed command; reading it after another command gives that newer status.

questions.q: A command that succeeds exits with code...
questions.e: Zero = success is the Unix convention.

questions.q: A correct if-statement skeleton is...
questions.e: if ...; then ...; fi - and mind the spaces inside [ ].

questions.q: Compare two strings for equality with...
questions.e: = compares strings; -eq is only for integers.

questions.q: Which test checks that a regular file exists?
questions.e: -f file exists and is regular; -d tests directories; -x tests executable.

questions.q: A for loop over servers looks like...
o: loop s in web1 web2; echo $s
for s in web1 web2; do echo $s; done
foreach s web1 web2; echo $s; end
questions.e: for name in list; do ...; done - the list can also come from $(...).

questions.q: A while loop needs which keywords?
questions.e: while condition; do body; done - e.g. while read -r line.

questions.q: Best structure for many pattern branches (start|stop|restart)...
questions.e: case matches patterns like start) ... ;; stop) ... ;; esac.

questions.q: Define a function in bash with...
questions.e: name() { commands; } then call it by name.

questions.q: Comments in bash start with...
questions.e: Everything after # on a line is ignored (except the shebang).

questions.q: In bash, what does set -e usually do for an unhandled failing simple command?
o: Exit the shell, with exceptions in conditions and command chains
questions.e: set -e exits on many unhandled failures, but not in several if/while tests, !, &&/|| chains and other contexts. Test error handling explicitly.

questions.q: The classic way to process a file line by line is...
o: while read -r line; do ...; done < file
questions.e: while read handles spaces safely; for over $(cat) splits on whitespace.

questions.q: echo "$HOME" vs echo '$HOME' differ because...
o: Double quotes expand variables; single quotes keep text literal
questions.e: Single quotes protect everything; double quotes allow $ expansion.

questions.q: PATH contains...
o: Directories the shell searches for commands
questions.e: When you type ls, the shell checks each PATH directory in order.

questions.q: Debug a script by printing each command before running it with...
questions.e: -x (xtrace) traces execution - the first debugging tool to reach for.

chapters.title: Boot, systemd & Services
chapters.desc: GRUB, systemctl, unit files and journalctl

questions.q: On a systemd-based Linux system, which program normally runs as PID 1?
questions.e: On a systemd-based installation, systemd is PID 1 and manages units. Other Linux init systems exist.

questions.q: BIOS/UEFI's role at boot is to...
o: Initialize hardware and hand over to the bootloader
questions.e: Firmware finds a bootable device and loads the bootloader from it.

questions.q: Which widely used bootloader commonly loads Linux kernels on PCs?
questions.e: GRUB is widely used, but systemd-boot and other bootloaders are also valid choices. The question asks for a common one.

questions.q: The correct boot order is...
questions.e: UEFI loads GRUB, GRUB loads the kernel, the kernel starts systemd.

questions.q: Start the nginx service immediately with...
questions.e: start acts now; enable only affects future boots.

questions.q: Make nginx start automatically at boot with...
questions.e: enable creates the symlink systemd checks at boot.

questions.q: Enable AND start a service in one command...
questions.e: --now combines enable + start.

questions.q: Which command shows a systemd service state and some recent journal lines by default?
questions.e: systemctl status nginx shows current state and recent journal entries when available; journalctl -u nginx gives a fuller log history.

questions.q: Which command lists loaded service units and their current state (inactive units need --all)?
questions.e: systemctl list-units --type=service lists loaded service units; --all includes inactive loaded units. To list installed unit files, use list-unit-files.

questions.q: Check if nginx is enabled at boot without starting anything...
questions.e: is-enabled reports enabled/disabled; is-active reports running state.

questions.q: Where should administrator-managed systemd system unit files and overrides usually go?
questions.e: /etc/systemd/system is the administrator location. Vendor units commonly live in /usr/lib/systemd/system or /lib/systemd/system.

questions.q: A unit file's three classic sections are...
questions.e: Unit=description/dependencies, Service=how to run, Install=boot wiring.

questions.q: In a service unit, what does WantedBy=multi-user.target typically specify for systemctl enable?
o: It runs once at install time
Start this service when the system boots to multi-user mode
questions.e: WantedBy tells enable where to install the wants symlink. Enabling the unit makes it start when that target is activated, subject to other unit settings.

questions.q: After changing a systemd unit file on disk, which command makes the manager reload unit definitions?
questions.e: daemon-reload makes systemd re-read unit definitions; restart the affected service separately if the running process must pick up changes.

questions.q: View logs collected by systemd with...
questions.e: journalctl queries the systemd journal - the modern log store.

questions.q: Logs for just the nginx unit with...
questions.e: -u filters the journal by unit name.

questions.q: Follow new journal entries live (like tail -f) with...
questions.e: -f streams entries as they arrive.

questions.q: See logs from the current boot only with...
questions.e: -b limits to this boot; -b -1 shows the previous boot.

questions.q: In systemd, runlevels were replaced by...
questions.e: Targets like multi-user.target group units like runlevels did.

questions.q: multi-user.target is roughly equivalent to old runlevel...
questions.e: Runlevel 3 = full multi-user without GUI; 5 added graphics.

questions.q: graphical.target corresponds to runlevel...
questions.e: Runlevel 5 = multi-user with a graphical login.

questions.q: Shut the system down immediately with...
questions.e: shutdown now (or poweroff) stops services cleanly and powers off.

questions.q: Reboot the machine with...
questions.e: reboot = shutdown -r; both restart the system cleanly.

questions.q: See which target the system boots into by default with...
questions.e: get-default shows the symlinked default target.

questions.q: Normally, what does systemctl mask nginx prevent that disable does not?
o: Mask only hides it from list
A masked unit cannot be started at all, even manually
questions.e: Masking links the unit to /dev/null, preventing ordinary activation, including manual start, until unmasked. Running instances may continue until stopped.

chapters.title: Security, Logs & Scheduled Tasks
chapters.desc: SSH keys, cron, tar/rsync and hardening basics

questions.q: With SSH key auth, the PUBLIC key goes...
questions.e: The server keeps your public key; you guard the private key.

questions.q: Generate an SSH key pair with...
questions.e: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 is the modern default choice.

questions.q: Install your public key on a remote host in one step with...
questions.e: ssh-copy-id appends your public key to the server's authorized_keys.

questions.q: Disable direct root login over SSH by setting...
questions.e: Edit sshd_config, then reload sshd; keep a sudo-capable user ready.

questions.q: System and application logs traditionally live in...
questions.e: /var/log/syslog (or journal), auth.log, nginx/ and more.

questions.q: On Debian/Ubuntu, where are SSH authentication events often recorded, if traditional auth logging is enabled?
questions.e: /var/log/auth.log is common on Debian-family systems; RHEL often uses /var/log/secure. Journal-based systems may use journalctl -u ssh or sshd.

questions.q: Show recent login history with...
questions.e: last reads wtmp: who logged in, when, from where.

questions.q: See who is logged in right now with...
questions.e: who (or w) lists current sessions with terminals and origins.

questions.q: Edit your personal cron schedule with...
questions.e: crontab -e opens your user crontab and installs it on save.

questions.q: The five cron time fields are...
questions.e: m h dom mon dow - then the command.

questions.q: Cron entry '*/5 * * * *' runs...
questions.e: */5 in the minute field = every five minutes.

questions.q: Cron entry '0 2 * * *' runs...
questions.e: minute 0, hour 2, every day - the classic backup slot.

questions.q: The cron shortcut for once a day is...
questions.e: @daily (= 0 0 * * *), @hourly, @weekly, @reboot also exist.

questions.q: System-wide cron drop-in directories include...
questions.e: Packages drop jobs into /etc/cron.d, cron.daily, cron.weekly...

questions.q: Create a gzipped tar archive of /etc with...
questions.e: c=create, z=gzip, f=file.

questions.q: Extract a .tar.gz archive with...
questions.e: x=extract, z=gzip, f=file; add -C to choose the target dir.

questions.q: List an archive's contents without extracting with...
questions.e: t=list - always peek before extracting unknown archives.

questions.q: Compress a single file with...
questions.e: gzip file creates file.gz and removes the original.

questions.q: Efficiently sync a directory to a remote host with...
questions.e: rsync transfers only what changed and preserves permissions with -a.

questions.q: Which common permission mode keeps an SSH private key readable and writable only by its owner?
questions.e: 600 makes the private key readable/writable by its owner only. 400 (owner read only) can also be safe; public-read mode 644 is not.

questions.q: fail2ban protects servers by...
o: Banning IPs after repeated failed logins
questions.e: fail2ban watches logs and firewall-bans brute-forcers.

questions.q: The principle of least privilege means...
o: Give users and services only the access they need
questions.e: Minimal rights limit the damage when something breaks or is attacked.

questions.q: Which routine action helps reduce exposure to already-fixed server vulnerabilities?
questions.e: Apply security updates regularly: patched software closes known flaws. Updates alone are not a guarantee of security.

questions.q: SELinux and AppArmor are...
o: Mandatory access control systems confining what processes may do
questions.e: MAC systems confine even root-owned daemons to their policy.

questions.q: scp to a server whose SSH runs on port 2222 uses...
questions.e: scp uses capital -P for port (ssh uses lowercase -p).
